title: Heavy rain for south Bengal until Saturday as Akvan crosses Odisha coast; dry from Tuesday
dek: The Kolkata weather office forecasts 7-20 cm at one or two places in seven districts, including both 24 Parganas and Howrah, until Saturday morning. Kalyani, Amta and Barrackpore recorded 9 cm in the past day.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Seven south Bengal districts, including North and South 24 Parganas and Howrah, face heavy to very heavy rain of 7-20 cm at one or two places until Saturday morning, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Kolkata said in its 12.30 pm special bulletin on Friday, after Cyclone Akvan crossed the Odisha coast near Gopalpur between 7.30 am and 8.30 am. Kolkata and the rest of south Bengal are forecast heavy rain of 7-11 cm at one or two places.

The storm is weakening as it moves north-north-east across Odisha and is expected to be a depression by Friday evening, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said. Rain should ease from Saturday: the RMC forecasts heavy rain only in Murshidabad on Saturday, light rain on Sunday and Monday, and dry weather across south Bengal from 24 November.

## Rain so far

In the 24 hours to 8.30 am on Friday, Kalyani in Nadia, Kalaikunda in West Midnapore, Amta in Howrah and Barrackpore in North 24 Parganas each recorded 9 cm, the RMC said, and Contai in East Midnapore 8 cm. Midnapore, Jhargram, Tarakeswar, Uluberia, Kharagpur and Basirhat each recorded 7 cm. Kolkata itself received 19.2 mm in the same period, according to reports. Rain disrupted public transport in the city during Friday's morning rush, and waterlogging had been reported on Thursday on College Street and Amherst Street and in Behala, Maniktala, Salt Lake and New Town, according to reports.

Until 8.30 am on Saturday, the RMC expects heavy to very heavy rain at one or two places in North 24 Parganas, South 24 Parganas, East Midnapore, West Midnapore, Jhargram, Bankura and Howrah, with thunderstorms and gusts of 40-50 kmph in South 24 Parganas and East Midnapore and 30-40 kmph elsewhere. It warned of temporary waterlogging in low-lying areas and underpasses, some damage to standing crops, kutcha roads and vulnerable houses, and a moderate risk of sudden local flooding in isolated pockets of East and West Midnapore, Bankura, Howrah, Nadia and the two 24 Parganas. It advised that harvested paddy be kept in a safe place and that beach activities be regulated on Friday. Squally winds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph are expected along the Bengal coast until Friday, and fishermen have been told not to go into the north-west Bay of Bengal until Saturday morning.

## Thursday's warnings

On Thursday, the RMC had put Kolkata, Howrah, Hooghly and North 24 Parganas under a heavy rain warning for Thursday and Friday and brought forward very heavy rain for South 24 Parganas and East Midnapore. It raised the signal at the Kolkata and Haldia ports to local cautionary signal No. 3.

## Flash-flood risk

In its 5.30 pm national bulletin on Thursday, the IMD flagged a moderate risk of flash floods over the next 24 hours in a few watersheds of five Gangetic West Bengal districts: East Midnapore, Howrah, North 24 Parganas, South 24 Parganas and Nadia. It said heavy to very heavy rain was very likely at isolated places in Gangetic West Bengal on Thursday and Friday, with heavy rain at isolated places on Saturday. Squally winds of 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph are expected along and off the Bengal coast until Friday noon, with very rough to high seas.

At 2.30 pm the storm lay about 470 km south of Puri, moving north at 13 kmph. The IMD's track now takes its remnants north over Odisha into Jharkhand, as a deep depression by Friday night and a well-marked low by Saturday, which keeps south-western Bengal districts such as Bankura, Purulia and Jhargram on the wetter side of the system.

## At sea

Squally winds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph are expected along and off the West Bengal coast on Thursday and Friday, with very rough to high seas, the RMC said. Over the north-west Bay of Bengal, winds are expected to strengthen to gale force, 70-80 kmph gusting to 90 kmph, until Friday noon. Fishermen have been told not to venture into the sea along the Bengal coast until 20 November; the IMD's latest bulletin extends its advice for the north-west and west-central Bay until Saturday morning, 21 November. The warnings matter for the trawler fleets of Digha, Kakdwip, Namkhana and Frasergunj, which work these waters, and the signal at Sagar Island has been raised to sectional signal No. II.

## Why it matters for Bengal

Rain in the second half of November comes as the aman paddy crop, south Bengal's main rice crop, approaches harvest, and as potato planting begins in districts such as Hooghly and Paschim Medinipur; heavy rain at this stage can flatten ripe paddy and waterlog fields. Bengal escaped the worst of Cyclone Arnab and Cyclone Murasu, which hit Andhra Pradesh and Odisha in late October and early November. In Odisha, about 3.7 lakh people were moved out of vulnerable areas ahead of Akvan's landfall, according to reports.

## What happens next

The RMC in Kolkata updates its special bulletins as the storm moves, and the IMD issues national bulletins every three hours. The heaviest rain for south Bengal is forecast for Friday and Friday night. The Declaration will update this story as forecasts for Bengal are revised.
